name: On the road
desc: Flat tyre, jump-start, warning lights, motorway breakdown, car kit, snow and heat, bike repairs

s: Get off the road onto firm, flat ground, hazard lights on. Put on a reflective vest (required in Italy when you get out on the road).
Put out the warning triangle well behind the car (in Italy at least 50 m). Handbrake on, in gear or Park.
Loosen the wheel nuts half a turn while the wheel is still on the ground.
Put the jack under the jacking point (see the manual or the mark on the sill) and lift until the wheel is off the ground.
Take off the nuts and the wheel, put on the spare, tighten the nuts by hand, crosswise.
Lower the car, then tighten the nuts firmly, crosswise. Check the spare's pressure soon; a thin space-saver is for max 80 km/h.
d: Never put any part of your body under a car on a jack
No tyre change on the motorway lane side: call for help

s: Park the good car close, engines off. Check both batteries are the same voltage (12 V in normal cars).
Red cable: + of the flat battery, then + of the good battery.
Black cable: − of the good battery, then a bare metal part of the engine of the dead car, away from the battery.
Start the good car and let it run a few minutes. Then start the dead car.
Remove the cables in the reverse order (black first).
Drive for at least 30 minutes to charge the battery. Won't start? The battery may need replacing.
d: Don't let the clamps touch each other
No smoking or flames near a battery

guides.w: A light comes on while driving
s: Red light: stop safely as soon as possible and switch off the engine.
Red oil can: oil pressure. Red thermometer: engine too hot. Red battery: not charging. Red brake symbol: brake problem.
Orange light: drive on carefully and get it checked soon.
Orange engine: engine fault (if it flashes, drive gently and stop soon). Orange tyre with “!”: tyre pressure.
Look up an unknown symbol in the car's manual (often also in the glovebox).
d: Don't open a hot radiator cap

guides.w: The car stops on a fast road
s: Hazard lights on and steer onto the hard shoulder or emergency lane, as far right as you can.
Put on your vest before getting out, and leave the car on the passenger side.
Everyone gets out and goes behind the crash barrier, well away from the car.
Italy: put the triangle at least 50 m behind, if you can do it safely. Netherlands: only if it's safe.
Call roadside assistance, or 112 if you're in a dangerous spot. Italian motorways have SOS phones every 2 km.
Wait behind the barrier, not in the car.
d: Don't stay in the car on the hard shoulder
Don't try repairs on the traffic side

guides.t: What to keep in the car
guides.w: Pack it once, then forget about it
s: A reflective vest for everyone (in reach of the seats) and a warning triangle.
A first-aid kit, a torch and jump cables.
A tyre repair kit or a spare wheel that's pumped up.
Water, a few snacks, a blanket, and a phone charging cable.
A paper road map.
Winter: an ice scraper and de-icer; in Italy snow chains or winter tyres on many roads from 15 November to 15 April.

guides.w: In the car for a long time
s: Stuck in snow: stay with the car. It's shelter and easier to find than you.
Run the engine about 10 minutes every hour for heat, and keep the exhaust free of snow (carbon monoxide).
Open a window a crack, wear everything warm, and move your arms and legs.
Make the car visible: a bright cloth on the aerial, the light inside on when the engine runs.
In heat: never leave children or pets in a parked car, not even for a few minutes. Find shade, open doors, drink.
Call 112 if anyone gets unwell.
d: Don't run the engine with snow blocking the exhaust

s: Take the wheel out (or work with it in place if needed) and let all the air out.
Push tyre levers under the tyre edge, hook one on a spoke, and run the other round to free one side.
Pull out the tube and pump it a little. Find the hole by listening, or in a bowl of water (bubbles).
Feel carefully inside the tyre for the thorn or glass that caused it, and remove it.
Roughen the area with the sandpaper, spread a thin layer of glue, wait until it's no longer shiny, then press the patch on hard.
Put the tube back slightly inflated, push the tyre edge back by hand, and pump it to the pressure printed on the side.
d: Don't use a screwdriver to lever the tyre: it makes a new hole

s: Stop and put the bike on its stand or upside down.
Hook the chain onto the bottom teeth of the front chainring.
Slowly turn the pedals backwards (or lift the back wheel and turn forwards): the chain runs back on.
On a bike with a chain guard (many Dutch bikes), loosen the back wheel slightly to get slack.
Keeps coming off? The chain is too loose or worn: get it adjusted.
A drop of oil on each link once a month keeps it smooth.

guides.t: Cycling safely in wind, rain and dark
s: Lights on when it's dark or misty: white in front, red at the back. In the Netherlands it's the law, with a fine.
In the wet: brake earlier and gently, and avoid painted lines, manhole covers and leaves.
Cross tram rails at an angle, never along them.
Strong headwind: shift to a light gear, bend lower, and ride behind someone in turns.
Crosswind gusts near bridges and gaps between buildings: hold the handlebars firmly and ride a bit away from the edge.
d: Don't ride with headphones in both ears in traffic
